title: Proactive demotion + FairPlay allocator for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Under mixed workloads we observe wide variance in P95/P99 token latency and tenant-level unfairness when GPU pools saturate. Current behavior is binary: we either admit requests into the high-performance kernel path or queue/reject. This leads to volatile tails for latency-sensitive tenants and wasted throughput for cost-sensitive tenants.

Proposal: Implement a "Proactive Demotion + FairPlay" allocator that: (1) pre-computes soft-demote candidates at admit time based on token-length distribution, tenant QoS, kernel availability and attention cost estimates; (2) instead of hard-dropping, routes demoted requests to alternative execution variants (quantized kernel, lower-attention-precision path, companion smaller model) or schedules fragmented prefill/decode across micro-slices to preserve fairness; (3) maintains a tenant-level budget and a sliding fairness window so long-running heavy tenants cannot monopolize high-performance kernels.

Key ideas to combine with runtime features:
- Kernel selection hints: use lightweight attn-cost estimator to prefer kernels optimized for long-context or sparse-attn on demoted requests.
- Attention optimizations: for demoted prefill, enable aggressive KV pruning, prefix caching reuse, and attention-sparsity fallbacks.
- Phase-splitting strategy: split prefill into progressive checkpoints so the scheduler can fill gaps with low-latency decode slices.
- Fairness policy: proportional allocation based on recent token-share and latency-SLO deficit (FairPlay scoring).
acceptance_criteria: 1) P95 token latency for latency-tier customers improves by >=10% under synthetic mixed workload (50% high-priority short requests, 50% long throughput requests)
2) Tenant fairness metric (max slowdown ratio vs baseline) is reduced by >=25% during 95th percentile congestion windows
3) End-to-end throughput degrades by <=6% compared to no-demotion baseline in same hardware footprint
4) No increase in error/incorrect-generation rate attributable to demotion paths >1% (measured via automated eval prompts)
5) Telemetry surfaces per-tenant demotion counts, demotion type (quantized/kernel variant/companion model), and attention-cost-savings; dashboards created in Console
